why: the representation predictor's own household configuration uses today, written as a pipeline spec so the same fitting tool can run it. Its source is the governed DEV resource e1_household_dev_pilot_v1 (DATA.json: window 60, horizon 60, the seven meter columns as ONE input block) and the design of tools/df_e1_pilot.py, whose core is 'tcn_w'. That core is native df_e1 code and is not a predictor.plugins entry point, so the closest DECLARED plugin is used here: the fusing core 'fused_branches' with a SINGLE branch holding every column and its 'tcn' encoder (dilated causal residual Conv1D blocks). What differs from the laya_chosen stage is therefore the representation and the grouping, not the plugin family.

why.windows: 60: the window the household DEV resource e1_household_dev_pilot_v1 declares (DATA.json 'window'), fixed by hand before any of this work
why.transform: level: the household pilot forecasts the level of Global_active_power
why.lags: none beyond the window itself; the hand configuration declares no lag features
why.features: none: the hand configuration adds no calendar or derived feature

grouping.why: the hand configuration feeds every meter column to one encoder; there is no grouping step in it

core.why: the household pilot's core is 'tcn_w' in native df_e1 code, which no predictor.plugins entry point names; the declared plugin closest to it is 'fused_branches' with one branch and its 'tcn' encoder

all.mapped_by: hand, from the household pilot's core_kind 'tcn_w'
all.why: 'tcn' is the dilated causal residual Conv1D family of 'fused_branches', the inline family closest to the pilot's tcn_w core
